images.note: 1917 Harris & Ewing portrait, cataloged 'BARUCH, BERNARD M., CHAIRMAN, WAR INDUSTRIES BOARD'. Contemporary likeness for the WIB beat (Baruch ran the WIB; Princeton review calls its success 'mixed'). Master TIFF 3834x5188 (~20MB); pipeline converts via ffmpeg.
images.title: Bernard M. Baruch, Chairman, War Industries Board (1917)

images.note: 1917 U.S. Food Administration poster: 'Food will win the war - We observe meatless days, wheatless days...' Exact match for the script beat (Hoover's voluntary pledges, Meatless Mondays/Wheatless Wednesdays, no ration books). Master TIFF 7008x4640 (~97MB); pipeline converts via ffmpeg.
images.title: Food will win the war - meatless days, wheatless days poster (1917)

images.note: 1918 Liberty Bond poster ('Have you bought your liberty bond'). Covers the bond-drive beat (four drives ~$17B, two-thirds of war costs; CPI celebrity pitches/quota races). Master TIFF 7713x11515 (~266MB); pipeline converts via ffmpeg.
images.title: Have you bought your liberty bond poster (1918)

images.note: NAACP Silent Protest Parade, New York City, July 28, 1917 - held in direct response to the East St. Louis riot (July 1917; official toll 39 Black / 9 white killed). Contemporary to the script beat; stronger than a generic riot photo. Master TIFF 6214x5172 (~96MB); pipeline converts via ffmpeg.
images.title: Silent protest parade in New York against the East St. Louis riots (1917)

images.note: National Woman's Party pickets at the White House, January 1917 (Alice Paul's NWP began picketing Jan 1917, before the war touched American soil). Direct match for the suffrage beat. Master TIFF 1536x1166 (~1.8MB); pipeline converts via ffmpeg.
images.title: Suffragette pickets at the White House (January 1917)

images.note: Harry R. Hopps, 'Destroy this mad brute Enlist - U.S. Army', ca. 1917 (LOC LC-DIG-ds-03216). The exact poster the script's AP stimulus question is built around (gorilla in German helmet, 'Destroy This Mad Brute: Enlist'). Master TIFF 9612x13868 (~400MB); pipeline converts via ffmpeg. No second institution found with a >=1200px scan (Smithsonian GAC scan is 857x1200; JHU 729x1024).
images.title: Destroy this mad brute Enlist - U.S. Army (Hopps, ca. 1917)

images.alt_source: Smithsonian American Art Museum (James Montgomery Flagg, I Want You for U.S. Army, 1917, chromolithograph; 1995.84.53)
images.note: James Montgomery Flagg, 'I want you for U.S. Army: nearest recruiting station', 1917 - the pointing Uncle Sam poster Maya's grandpa has in his garage. Master TIFF 12256x16464 (~605MB); pipeline converts via ffmpeg. Largest file in catalog; download is one-time.
images.title: I want you for U.S. Army - Flagg Uncle Sam poster (1917)

images.alt_source: Smithsonian National Portrait Gallery (Eugene Victor Debs by Carlo de Fornaro, 1911; NPG.90.117)
images.note: Half-length portrait of Eugene Victor Debs, dated 1912 - pre-war likeness, honestly labeled. Used for the Debs beat (10-year sentence under 1917 Espionage Act, 1920 run from prison, ~913,693 votes, release Christmas Day 1921). The 1921 Atlanta-release photos at LOC have no digital file. Master TIFF 3313x4096 (~13.5MB); pipeline converts via ffmpeg.
images.title: Eugene Victor Debs, half-length portrait (1912)
